introduction.heading: What is Express.js?
introduction.description: Express is a minimal, unopinionated web framework for Node.js. Node's built-in http module gives you a raw request/response pair and leaves everything else - routing, parsing bodies, serving files, handling errors - up to you. Express wraps that in a small, composable API: you describe routes, stack up middleware functions to handle cross-cutting concerns (logging, auth, parsing), and Express takes care of matching incoming requests to the right handler and running everything in order.

concepts.title: Routing
concepts.description: Map an HTTP method + path (app.get('/users/:id', ...)) to a handler function

concepts.title: Middleware
concepts.description: Functions that run in sequence for a request, each able to inspect/modify it and call next()

concepts.title: Request & Response
concepts.description: req wraps the incoming request (params, query, body, headers); res builds the reply

concepts.title: Router
concepts.description: express.Router() groups related routes into their own mini-app you can mount at a path

concepts.title: Error Handling
concepts.description: A special 4-argument middleware (err, req, res, next) catches errors passed to next(err)

pipeline.heading: The Middleware Pipeline
pipeline.description: Every request Express receives travels through a chain of middleware functions, in the exact order they were registered with app.use()/app.get()/etc. Each function can respond, modify the request, or hand off to the next one by calling next() - if it never calls next() (and doesn't send a response), the request just hangs. This ordered chain is the single most important thing to understand about Express: authentication middleware has to run before the routes it protects, error handlers have to be registered last, and a middleware that forgets next() silently breaks everything after it.

gettingStarted.heading: Getting Started
steps: Create an app with const app = express() and add middleware with app.use()
Parse JSON request bodies with app.use(express.json())
Split routes into express.Router() modules as the app grows

practiceTopics.title: Routing & Route Params
practiceTopics.description: Match HTTP methods and paths, and read dynamic segments and query strings

practiceTopics.title: Request & Response
practiceTopics.description: Read from req and build replies with res.json, res.status, res.send

practiceTopics.title: express.Router()
practiceTopics.description: Group related routes into their own module and mount them on the app

practiceTopics.description: Turn raw request bytes into req.body with express.json() and express.urlencoded()

fullExample.heading: Full Example, Step by Step
fullExample.title: A small REST API: routing, middleware, and error handling together
fullExample.description: This example ties the core concepts above into one realistic file: a users API with logging middleware, a modular router, JSON parsing, and centralized error handling. Click through the steps to see which lines each one is talking about.

steps.label: Create the app
steps.explanation: require("express") returns a function; calling it gives you an app object with .get/.post/.use/.listen - the core of every Express server.

steps.label: Parse JSON bodies
steps.explanation: express.json() is built-in middleware that reads the raw request stream and, if the Content-Type is application/json, parses it into req.body for every route below this line.

steps.label: Log every request
steps.explanation: app.use() with no path runs this middleware for every request, in the order it was registered. Calling next() is what lets the request continue to whatever's next in the chain.

steps.label: Group routes with a Router
steps.explanation: express.Router() creates a self-contained set of routes - a mini Express app - that can be developed, tested, and mounted independently of the main app.

steps.label: Read a route param
steps.explanation: req.params.id comes from the :id segment in the route path. Passing an object to next() skips straight to the error handler instead of continuing normally.

steps.label: Read the parsed body
steps.explanation: Because express.json() ran earlier in the chain, req.body.name is already a parsed value here - no manual stream reading required.

steps.label: Mount the router
steps.explanation: app.use("/users", usersRouter) prefixes every route inside usersRouter with /users, so GET "/" inside the router becomes GET /users.

steps.label: Catch unmatched routes
steps.explanation: Middleware registered after all the routes only runs if nothing above matched - a catch-all 404.

steps.label: Handle every error in one place
steps.explanation: A middleware function with exactly 4 parameters (err, req, res, next) is treated specially by Express as an error handler, and only runs when next(err) is called anywhere upstream.

steps.label: Start listening
steps.explanation: listen(port, callback) starts the server and keeps the process alive, accepting connections on the given port.
